record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Every degree of decidable categoricity is a degree of categoricity. Is the converse true: must every degree of categoricity also occur as a degree of decidable categoricity? The paper notes in particular the cases of degrees at or above 0^(α) for large computable ordinals α, and asks what happens for d.c.e. degrees.

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Every degree of decidable categoricity is a degree of categoricity. Is the converse true? A conjecture for this problem is that it is true for d ≥ 0(α), where α is 'sufficiently large' computable ordinal. Say, for α = ω. What happens with d.c.e. degrees d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Work in the setting of computable structure theory. A countable structure $\mathcal{A}$ in a computable language is called computable if its domain is $\omega$ and all its atomic relations and functions are uniformly computable; it is called decidable if its elementary diagram is computable. For a Turing degree $\mathbf{d}$, a structure $\mathcal{A}$ is $\mathbf{d}$-computably categorical if for any two computable copies $\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C}$ of $\mathcal{A}$ there is a $\mathbf{d}$-computable isomorphism $\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{C}$; similarly, $\mathcal{A}$ is $\mathbf{d}$-decidably categorical if for any two decidable copies $\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C}$ of $\mathcal{A}$ there is a $\mathbf{d}$-computable isomorphism between them.

The degree of categoricity of a computable structure $\mathcal{A}$ is, when it exists, the least Turing degree $\mathbf{d}$ such that $\mathcal{A}$ is $\mathbf{d}$-computably categorical. The degree of decidable categoricity of a decidable structure $\mathcal{A}$ is, when it exists, the least Turing degree $\mathbf{d}$ such that $\mathcal{A}$ is $\mathbf{d}$-decidably categorical. A Turing degree is called a degree of categoricity (respectively, a degree of decidable categoricity) if it arises in this way from some computable (respectively, decidable) structure.

It is known that every degree of decidable categoricity is a degree of categoricity.

Questions.

(1) Is the converse true? That is, does every degree of categoricity arise as the degree of decidable categoricity of some decidable structure?

(2) In particular, for a "sufficiently large" computable ordinal $\alpha$ (for instance $\alpha = \omega$), is it true that every Turing degree $\mathbf{d} \geq \mathbf{0}^{(\alpha)}$ which is a degree of categoricity is also a degree of decidable categoricity?

(3) What is the answer when one restricts attention to d.c.e. degrees $\mathbf{d}$ (Turing degrees of differences of two computably enumerable sets)?
artifact.category_tag: Computable structure theory: degrees of categoricity
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returns only general results on degrees of categoricity and decidable categoricity (Csima et al., Goncharov, Downey–Kach–Lempp, and related works), but no source establishing the converse — that every degree of categoricity is a degree of decidable categoricity — either in general, for cones above $\mathbf{0}^{(\alpha)}$, or for d.c.e. degrees. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Degrees of Categoricity and the Hyperarithmetic Hierarchy
status_evidence.snippet: Defines degrees of categoricity and shows every degree of categoricity is hyperarithmetic; does not resolve the converse with decidable categoricity.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference on degrees of categoricity without resolving the converse question.

status_evidence.title: On Decidable Categoricity and Almost Prime Models
status_evidence.snippet: Studies degrees of decidable categoricity for almost prime models.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on degrees of decidable categoricity that does not establish the converse in general.

status_evidence.title: Decidable Categoricity Spectra for Almost Prime Models
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) study of decidable categoricity spectra; the general converse problem is not settled here.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the area is still active and the general problem remains open.
